text: Grandparents had cheap needs and expensive wants. Today it's the reverse.
Black Friday: 30% off. January: 100% of it is due.

A family health insurance plan through work now costs $28,303 a year.

The employer covers about $20,833.
The worker pays $7,471. That part jumped 9% in ONE year.

For perspective: $28,303 is almost two full years of pay at the federal minimum wage.

Here's the part nobody explains at review time:

That $20,833 is part of the compensation budget.

When premiums climb, there's less left over for raises.

So when the raise comes in at "only" 3%, some of it already went to the insurance company.

And the deductible still hasn't been met.

This is the most expensive November for gas on record.

National average: $3.91 a gallon.
This time last year: $3.08.

Fill up a 15-gallon tank once a week:

Last year: $46.20
This year: $58.65

That's $12.45 more every single fill-up.

Over a year? About $647 more.

Same car. Same commute. Same job.

And not one raise came with a line item for gas.
